explanation: Grenade is French for pomegranate, and a pomegranate appears on the coat of arms of Granada, in Spain. Many cheap grenadines swap the fruit for other flavourings.

claims.text: Grenadine takes its name from the French grenade, pomegranate, and was traditionally made from pomegranate juice.
Grenadine was not traditionally made from cherries, raspberries or redcurrants.
Grenade is the French word for pomegranate.
A pomegranate appears on the coat of arms of the Spanish city of Granada.
Many commercial grenadine syrups use flavourings other than pomegranate.
